extracted.intended_audience: photographers entering the World Press Photo Contest (contest entrants, submitters, and their editors/representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Verification requirements and checks applied to contest submissions to ensure authenticity and compliance with the code of ethics and entry rules, including entry-level checks, manipulation review, fact-checking, caption disclosure, and story text verification. Also specifies original-file submission formats and consequences for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry checks for all entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Our team conducts several checks to ensure entries are in line with the entry rules and category requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks include verifying that only permitted formats are entered (e.g., where only single frame photographs can be entered to categories, checking for multiple exposures, polyptychs, stitched images), ensuring photographs do not contain added texts or added borders, confirming creation and publication dates comply with the rules, and spotting any upload problems that might have occurred when uploading to the entry platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on altering content of photographs (Entry Rule 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs “must not be altered by adding, rearranging, reversing, distorting or removing people and/or objects from within the frame.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the 'what counts as manipulation' page for full details and examples of unacceptable alterations. This prohibition is enforced during the manipulation review stage of the contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted minor edits (exceptions to manipulation rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two exceptions to the manipulation prohibition: (i) cropping that removes extraneous details is permitted; (ii) sensor dust or scratches on scans of negatives can be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other changes to content (adding/removing/rearranging elements) remain prohibited. When in doubt refer to the detailed 'what counts as manipulation' guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original file submission requirements for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants whose photographs progress are required to provide the file as recorded by the camera in an approved original format for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted originals: RAW file(s) (only 1 frame per contest image required); OR full format JPEG file(s) as delivered by the camera provided in a series showing at least seven frames (three frames before the contest entry, the contest frame, and three frames after); OR for smartphones, the unedited photograph emailed directly from the phone and provided in a series showing at least seven frames (three before, the contest image, three after); OR unprocessed unedited positive scans of film negatives plus a contact sheet showing at least seven frames. A visual guide to original file formats is provided. Failure to provide these files will lead to elimination of the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and contact for manipulation verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The manipulation verification process takes place during judging for entries eligible to progress; entrants are contacted to provide original files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants whose photographs remain in the contest and are eligible to progress are contacted between 26 January and 22 February 2026 to supply required originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection method: independent digital analyst comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Two independent digital analysts compare original files with contest entries to determine whether the content of any photograph (single photograph or a frame in a story) has been altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comparison assesses whether content has been added, removed, rearranged, reversed or distorted relative to the submitted contest image. This is part of the manipulation review process for later-round entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for non-compliance with file/verification requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to provide the requested original files or otherwise comply with verification requests will result in elimination of the entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elimination makes the entry ineligible for any possible award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking of winners' image context
rubrics_metrics.description: An external research team will check the context in which each winning image or story was produced, distributed and/or published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks could include whether persons named in the caption are in the photo, whether a news event can be confirmed to have taken place, whether an animal is correctly identified to species, whether the location is accurate, whether the date is correct, etc. Fact-checking also addresses clause 2 of the code of ethics concerning intent to mislead by recreating or staging events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption requirements and disclosure of photographer influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions must explain the circumstances in which a photograph was taken and disclose if the photographer influenced or directed the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the photographer influenced the scene in any way, or gave directions to a subject to pose in any way for a portrait, this must be disclosed in the caption. Captions provided by photographers are edited for accuracy and clarity, and are used as the base for fact-checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story text verification and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: After winners are selected, an external research team gathers background information for each photograph and story; World Press Photo is responsible for story text published in the yearbook, exhibition and website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers provide basic captions; if additional required information is missing or incorrect, photographers will be contacted and asked to provide correct information. Winning photographers are asked to fact check captions and story descriptions before publication.
